Content hash of a dataset payload

Source: R/save-objects.R
dataset_store.Rd

The dataset analogue of model_hash() / repository_hash(): a stable content hash of the payload with volatile attributes stripped. Works for data.frames (weather/demand tables), geoscales::GeoScale maps, and any other R object.

save_dataset() writes a payload — a data.frame (a weather or demand series), a geoscales::GeoScale map, or any R object — into the store <datasets_path>/<name>/ (see get_datasets_path()). An entry holds its versions by content: the payload of each version lives under <name>/<hash>/ and the entry's dataset.yml names the current version and lists every version present. Saving identical content again is a no-op; saving other content under the same name adds a version and makes it current, nothing is overwritten; saving content already stored as an older version makes that version current again. load_dataset() takes the current version by name, or a pinned one by hash (full or a prefix, also as name@hash). An entry written before versions, with its payload beside the manifest, reads as its single version. A stored dataset can then be REFERENCED by repositories, models, and scenarios instead of embedded — see the embed_datasets argument of save_repository(), save_model() and save_scenario(): the table is stored once, however many model or scenario versions use it.

A FUNCTIONAL dataset records a generating call instead of typed-in data: pass fun = "pkg::fun" and args = list(...) (no x). By default (materialize = TRUE) the call is evaluated once at save time and the result is stored as a snapshot: the dataset's identity is the CONTENT hash of that result, loading uses the snapshot without the generating package, and re-evaluation (load_dataset(evaluate = TRUE) on a functional entry) can verify the recorded result_hash — a mismatch warns (package drift is worth seeing), or errors with strict = TRUE. materialize = FALSE stores no snapshot and hashes the normalized call (hash_of: call in the manifest); loading then requires the package.

load_dataset() resolves by name (optionally "name@hash8", or with hash =) via the registry first, then by scanning the store; path bypasses resolution. It returns the bare payload.

Usage

dataset_hash(x)

save_dataset(
  x,
  name,
  fun = NULL,
  args = NULL,
  materialize = TRUE,
  path = NULL,
  registry = TRUE,
  format = get_storage_format(),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  rehash = TRUE,
  memo = "",
  hash = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

load_dataset(
  name,
  hash = NULL,
  path = NULL,
  evaluate = FALSE,
  strict = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

the dataset payload.

name

character, dataset name, "name@hash8", or a store directory path.

fun

character, a namespaced generator "pkg::fun" (functional datasets only).

args

list, yaml-serializable arguments of fun.

materialize

logical, evaluate fun at save time and store the result snapshot (default). FALSE records the call only.

path

character, explicit store directory.

registry

logical, add/refresh the registry row on save.

format

storage format for tables (as in save_scenario()).

overwrite

logical, rewrite the store entry even when the hash matches.

rehash

logical; FALSE keeps the DESTINATION entry's recorded hash while writing the changed content — for changes the user declares insignificant (a description, a memo). The manifest marks the exception (hash_kept: true); references then verify against the retained hash. With rehash = FALSE the hash is a user-managed version tag, not a content proof. A version referenced by another store entry is never rewritten: the save stops and names the dependents.

memo

character, optional registry note.

hash

character, full or short content hash to pin a version.

verbose

logical.

evaluate

logical, for a functional entry: re-evaluate the recorded call (verifying result_hash) instead of only reading the snapshot. Falls back to the snapshot with a message when the package is missing.

strict

logical, error (instead of warn) when a re-evaluated functional dataset no longer matches its recorded result_hash.

Value

character, the full hash (the store uses its first 8 characters).

save_dataset() returns list(name, hash, kind, path), invisibly. load_dataset() returns the payload.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
open_project(tempdir())

# a table a model refers to, stored once and referenced by hash
save_dataset(topia$weather, "topia_weather")
dataset_hash(topia$weather)
load_dataset("topia_weather")

# or store the CALL that makes it -- `fun` is a namespaced name, and the
# payload is left out entirely -- and materialize it on demand
save_dataset(name = "profiles", fun = "energyRt::topia_profiles",
             args = list(regions = c("W1", "W2")), materialize = FALSE)
load_dataset("profiles", evaluate = TRUE)
} # }
